source_supported: SNL267:009 lists eight M567 small brake-gear spring washers. No dimensions or free spring shape printed.
SNL220:023 lists five M564 tension springs: four control-rod applications and one fan jockey pulley. Only four control applications are modeled here.

SNL6 depicts return springs at the short foot/low-speed connections and raised bracket ears. HB104 shows the supporting rear-channel arrangement with transmission removed. Neither image resolves complete hook geometry.
approximations: M567 is modeled as a compressed annular spring washer, not a proved free flat washer. The eight selected short-connection pin positions are inferred from the SNL6 callouts; handbook quantity differs and is retained in the earlier source packet.

M564 front hook: a 300-degree eye around the fork socket, retained behind the existing jam nut. Chosen as a physically capturable control-rod attachment without changing established pin/receiver geometry. It is an explicit mounting hypothesis, not a recovered source detail.
M564 rear hook passes through the measured M4136 6.65 mm hole and contacts its -X wall; tip bends outside the cheek.

Wire diameter, coil diameter/count, lead shapes and static installed extension are estimates. Four geometry definitions represent installed states of one source part family, not four different catalogue parts. No inferred free-length, spring rate, material stress or motion qualification.
rejected: The Gemini spring front tips were not checked against any actual capture/seating interface; absence of collision is insufficient.
A 2.6 mm wire hook cannot fit in the 1.538 mm fork-to-cotter gap already occupied by a 1.5 mm washer. Do not silently increase the qualified pin grip.
validation_requirements: Actual seating/capture on jam-nut face and bracket bore; withdrawal/shift negatives.
No mating-pair exemptions in surrounding-material checks.
Full wire stock versus centerline; curvature/self-separation; native and installed STEP roundtrip.
Independent measured washer seat, complete bore passage and retention.
